verdict: Masco grew sales 3% and squeezed out much more profit — net income rose 16% to $230M as plumbing products sold well and margins widened, even with paint sales flat.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: +3% YoY (+4% excluding a divested business and currency)

kpis.label: Returned to shareholders
kpis.note: dividends and buybacks in the quarter

segments.name: Plumbing Products
segments.note: Faucets, shower systems and fittings (Delta, Hansgrohe, Brizo brands) — Masco's biggest business, growing 5% in local currency excluding a divested unit.

segments.name: Decorative Architectural Products
segments.note: Paint and coatings, mostly Behr — flat versus a year ago as home-improvement demand stayed soft.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling and back-office costs. The release reports $381M; $1M of rounding in the reported millions is absorbed here so the statement foots.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $29M, partly offset by $13M of other income, net.

takeaways.title: Plumbing carries the growth
takeaways.text: Plumbing Products sales rose 4% to $1.3B (5% in local currency before a divestiture), while paint and coatings were flat at $628M.

takeaways.title: Margins did the heavy lifting
takeaways.text: Adjusted operating margin widened to 17.9% from 15.9% a year ago — pricing and cost discipline turned 3% sales growth into 23% adjusted EPS growth.

takeaways.title: Cash keeps flowing back
takeaways.text: Masco returned $322M to shareholders in the quarter through dividends and share repurchases.

footerNote: Net income of $230M is the amount attributable to Masco; consolidated net income was $240M, with $10M belonging to noncontrolling interests.
